aboutAuthor: Robert G. Hagstrom is portfolio manager and author of The Warren Buffett Way. He decodes Buffett's evolution from Graham cigar butts to business-driven ownership via float and concentration.

points.heading: From cigar butt to wonderful business
points.body: Munger moved Buffett from buying fair businesses at wonderful prices to buying wonderful businesses at fair prices where reinvestment and pricing power compound longer than asset discounts.

points.heading: Float is structural alpha
points.body: Insurance premiums before claims give cost-free leverage that mutual funds lack, letting Berkshire fund moat purchases without fee drag or redemption pressure.

points.heading: Four-filter business check
points.body: Understandable, moated, owner-managed, and reinvestable — price matters only after these pass and you would own the whole business for ten years with market closed.

points.heading: Value evolves to owner earnings
points.body: Intrinsic value as discounted owner earnings justifies three times book for moats like See's and Apple where brand raises prices without extra capital.

points.heading: Active can win at Berkshire cost
points.body: Zero fee on float, sub ten percent turnover, and deferred tax let high-conviction ten-stock focus beat indexes where average active fails on cost and trading.

points.heading: Money mind triad
points.body: Sportsman scores, teacher clarifies, artist waits for fat pitches — integrating competitiveness, teaching, and patience is the ultimate capital allocation moat.

insights: Sidney farm mortgage at age fourteen where newspaper route savings bought 40 acres, first float compounding before high school.
See's $25 million purchase that tripled profit in ten years without capital via annual price hikes that defined wonderful business.
Berkshire's 45 percent drawdown in 2008 where buying while others sold proved deferred tax and float discipline.
conclusion: Inside the Ultimate Money Mind shows Buffett as sportsman, teacher, and artist who evolved value from net-nets to moats and funds it with float, offering a low-cost, high-conviction template for any owner-analyst.
